knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Lazy resource lifetime mismatch between upstream iterable sources and downstream buffered consumers
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Iterable data pipelines may yield lazily managed resources whose validity depends on upstream iterator state. If a downstream buffering or shuffling consumer exhausts and closes the upstream source before all previously yielded resources have been consumed, later consumption can fail with invalid-state or closed-resource errors.

risk_dimensions.execution_state: Upstream iterator exhaustion and closure occurs while downstream buffered consumers still hold unread yielded resources, causing delayed consumption to observe invalid resource state.

failure_mechanism.description: Iterable datapipes may return lazy resources such as file-like streams that remain tied to the lifetime of the originating iterator. When a downstream buffering or shuffling consumer requests more elements than the upstream source contains, the upstream iterator may be exhausted and closed before all previously yielded resources have been read, leading to use-after-close or stale stream access.

input_exploration: Explore iterable sources with small element counts paired with downstream buffering or shuffling consumers whose requested buffer size exceeds the upstream element count
Vary yielded resource sizes, including empty and large payloads
Vary source formats and internal structure when the iterable source is archive-like or container-like
Trigger delayed consumption of previously yielded resources only after the upstream source has been fully exhausted
constraint_awareness: Lazy resources yielded by an iterable source may remain tied to the source iterator's lifetime
Buffered consumers can prefetch and hold resources after the upstream iterator is exhausted
Exhausting or closing an upstream source may invalidate not-yet-consumed yielded resources
The relationship between downstream buffer size and upstream element count is a critical boundary
oracle_strategy: Detect exceptions raised when consuming previously yielded resources after upstream source exhaustion
Compare behavior against direct reads from the underlying source without buffered pipeline stages
Check for invalid stream states, closed handle errors, or stale resource access

transferability.reason: The principle applies broadly to iterable data pipelines that yield lazy resources such as file handles, streams, database cursors, or network iterators through buffering, shuffling, or prefetching stages. Transferability depends on whether the target APIs use similar lazy-resource lifetime contracts; eager materialization pipelines may not exhibit the issue.

important_considerations: Focus on lifecycle and exhaustion order in multi-stage data pipelines
Vary downstream buffer or prefetch sizes beyond the upstream source cardinality
Consume yielded resources only after the upstream source has been fully exhausted
Consider sources that return lazy handles or streams rather than eagerly materialized values
generation_strategy: Generate parameterized data pipeline harnesses that combine iterable sources with buffering or shuffling consumers under configurable cardinality and buffer sizes. Generalize away from archive-specific details to any resource-yielding iterable source, and use oracle checks for exceptions or stale resource states when reading delayed yielded elements.
